items.title: An Explainable Machine Learning Framework with Large Language Model Features for Predicting Monetary Redress in Bank Fraud and Scam Complaints
items.abstract: Liability for scam losses is shifting towards banks, yet few interpretable tools can anticipate which fraud and scam complaints will end in redress. This study develops SCAM-XD, an explainable framework that predicts whether a complaint to the US Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB) flagged as possible fraud or a scam closes with monetary relief reported by the company. From the CFPB narratives archive, the study builds a benchmark of these complaints, about half of which human coders confirm as fraud or scams. A large language model (LLM) codes each narrative for scam type, payment rail, authorisation, manipulation cues and signals of the bank's response, agreeing closely with human coding on scam type. These features are combined with structured fields, company identity and text representations in a stacking ensemble, explained with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) and linked to a cost-sensitive triage layer. Tested on a later period, SCAM-XD improves significantly on strong baselines across seeds, including a reimplemented topic model approach. LLM features yield a compact, interpretable model that nearly matches a high-dimensional text baseline but do not significantly improve the full model. Company identity is the strongest driver of predicted redress, yet firm identity alone predicts far less well, and payment rail and bank response cues act in directions consistent with liability rules. Under assumed costs, thresholds selected on validation data substantially reduce modelled expected cost relative to standard thresholds, whereas model choice matters much less. Redress depends on both the firm and the facts that determine liability.

items.title: An LLM-Agent-Based Dynamic Planning and Monitoring System in the Educational Domain
items.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are enabling conversational agents capable of supporting increasingly complex workflows beyond traditional question-answering. In education, collaborative projects require continuous planning, coordination, and monitoring, yet existing educational chatbots mainly focus on tutoring or administrative support. This paper presents vProjTutor , an LLM-agent-based project management system that assists student teams throughout the complete project lifecycle. The proposed architecture integrates specialized LLM agents with external project-management tools, including Telegram, Trello, and GitHub, allowing users to configure projects, organize tasks, generate Sprint plans, monitor progress, and interpret repository activity through natural language interactions. A user study involving ten participants evaluated usability, task completion, and user satisfaction. Participants achieved an overall task completion rate of 93.3%, and the system obtained an overall BUS usability score of 85%. However, the system correctly interpreted 60% of commit messages, highlighting the need for further improvements in handling unstructured inputs. The results suggest that LLM-agent-based architectures constitute a promising approach for supporting collaborative projects in educational environments.

items.title: Analisis Pendekatan Student-Centered Learning dalam Prespektif Psikologi Perkembangan di Sekolah Menengah Atas
items.abstract: This literature review study aims to analyze the implementation of a student-centered learning (SCL) approach based on developmental psychology in Senior High Schools (SMA). High school-age adolescents (15–18 years) are at the formal-operational cognitive development stage and are undergoing an intensive identity formation phase. These psychological characteristics demand a learning approach that is not only content-centered but also responsive to the developmental dynamics of students. Through a systematic literature review of scientific sources published between 2020 and 2025, this study found that effective SCL implementation in high schools requires: (1) learning planning based on the Zone of Proximal Development (ZPD) and needs differentiation; (2) implementation integrating Problem-Based Learning, Project-Based Learning, and Cooperative Learning models; and (3) authentic assessment measuring holistic competence. Findings indicate that SCL grounded in developmental psychology understanding significantly enhances students' intrinsic motivation, cognitive-emotional engagement, and learning independence. Critical factors determining implementation success include teachers' pedagogical competence, institutional support, and the availability of a psychologically safe learning environment.

items.title: Analyzing Eye-Tracking Indicators of Situation Awareness to Support Human-AI Teaming Under Varying Workload Conditions
items.abstract: Ensuring high levels of Situation awareness (SA) is essential for air traffic controllers (ATCOs), enabling them to continuously process and integrate information into a comprehensive understanding of the situation as it dynamically changes. In the context of human-automation collaboration, SA becomes even more critical, as operators must be prepared to take over control in emergency situations. Although existing studies have largely assessed SA as either poor or good, limited research has explored identification of SA levels (Level 1, 2, and 3). To investigate the potential of eye-tracking technology for real-time SA levels assessment, we conducted an SA-inducing experiment involving 18 participants. Participants are required to perform a series of air traffic control (ATC) tasks corresponding to three SA levels, while their eye-tracking data were simultaneously collected. Eye-tracking features are analyzed using a two-way repeated measures ANOVA. Results identified total fixation duration, number of fixations, average pupil diameter and average amplitude of saccades as key indicators for distinguishing SA levels. Additionally, our findings highlight a significant interaction between SA levels and workload, demonstrating that the effectiveness of these metrics varies under different workload conditions. These insights contribute to enhancing real-time SA evaluation in the safety-critical environments like ATC, further improving the overall operational efficiency and safety in various human-automation collaboration scenarios.

items.title: AR-WAM: efficient streaming world-action modeling for autonomous driving
items.abstract: Autonomous driving requires anticipating how traffic will evolve while responding quickly to new observations. Video foundation models offer the first ability, but repeated history encoding and iterative video generation make them costly to use for driving. We present AR-WAM, an efficient streaming world-action model that combines autoregressive temporal modeling with single-pass future conditioning. Because its video backbone is causal, AR-WAM updates its visual context incrementally, reusing past computation and conditioning future prediction on observed motion. We further hypothesize that future features computed from recent observations can improve generalization in dynamic traffic without iterative video generation. AR-WAM therefore obtains these features in one forward pass and uses them to condition trajectory generation, and reinforcement learning then improves the policy through direct optimization of driving rewards. With a single front camera, AR-WAM achieves 91.5 PDMS after supervised training and 94.0 after reinforcement learning on NAVSIM-v1, outperforming the compared strong end-to-end world-action models. In a dynamic setting of continuous driving, supervised AR-WAM keeps its visual history across decisions and outperforms strong world-action baselines.

items.title: Are neural studies held to a lower standard of sample-size justification? A confirmatory test with independent human coding
items.abstract: Are neural studies in psychology and neuroscience held to a lower standard of sample-size justification than behavioral studies, even when they use the same statistical tests? This registration specifies the confirmatory test of that claim. Exploratory findings. A large language model (Claude Opus 5.5), run with a fixed prompt, schema and codebook, screened 35,697 open-access articles published in 2025 in 308 JCR Q1 psychology and neuroscience journals and coded every eligible study's data type, main test, analyzed sample, stated minimum sample size and any justification of the sample size. Among 4,747 studies, neural studies stated a minimum sample size less often than behavioral studies and more often gave no justification of any kind. These findings rest on one automated measurement, checked so far only against itself; errors that differ between neural and behavioral studies could in principle produce them. Confirmatory test. Four human coders, blind to the model's codes, independently code a stratified random sample of 250 studies: 100 behavioral and 100 neural studies from the main analysis and 50 studies the model excluded from it. The sample is drawn by a registered rule and seed, studies are coded in random order, 50 studies are double-coded, and all coders first calibrate on 10 practice studies. We test (H1) whether neural studies still state a minimum less often and still more often give no justification after the full-sample rates are corrected for the coding errors measured against the human codes, and (H2) whether the automated coding agrees with human coding (κ ≥ .80; ICC ≥ .90 for sample size), a precondition for interpreting the full-sample results. Human codes are not treated as error-free: every disagreement is adjudicated. Expected outcomes. Corrected estimates of the two neural–behavioral gaps; agreement for each coded variable, overall and by data type; the model's error rates in each group; the rate at which the model wrongly excluded studies; and human–human reliability as a benchmark. If H1 holds, the gaps cannot be explained by coding error; if it fails, we will report that they cannot be distinguished from it. The pipeline, prompts, scripts and codes will be released openly for reuse and audit.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence for Automated Detection and Segmentation of Pulp Stones in Cone Beam Computed Tomography Scans.
items.abstract: Objective : This study aimed to automatically detect the human tooth pulp cavity and pulp stones on cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) using deep learning-based semantic segmentation. Methodology : 523 annotated images of teeth from 112 CBCT examinations were used to train and evaluate four established deep learning architectures (U-Net, Attention U-Net, U-Net++, and DeepLabV3+) in segmenting the background, pulp cavity, and pulp stone(s). Subsequently a novel architecture was developed (DACA-DeepLab) and evaluated through an additive study. DACA-DeepLab incorporates DeepLabV3+ with a pyramid channel-spatial attention (PCSA) module, a dual-axis cross-attention (DACA) decoder, and a Sobel-guided boundary-refinement (BFR) head. Results : DeepLabV3+ achieved the best overall Dice performance among the four baseline architectures (mean, 0.775; pulp cavity, 0.838; pulp stone, 0.711). In the second study, combining PCSA and DACA yielded the highest performance (mean Dice, 0.733). Adding the boundary-refinement head reduced performance, suggesting sensitivity to the limited training set. Conclusion : Deep learning-based semantic segmentation can accurately identify human tooth pulp cavity and pulp stone(s) on CBCT. These findings establish a systematic benchmark for CBCT-based pulp segmentation and provide a foundation for AI-assisted endodontic diagnosis and pre-treatment planning.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence in Middle and Secondary Education: Instructional Opportunities, Limitations and Ethical Considerations
items.abstract: Middle and secondary school educators should utilize and implement Artificial Intelligence (AI) as a support tool for instruction, not a replacement for their pedagogy and lesson planning. Utilizing and implementing AI can assist with lesson planning, differentiation, feedback, and generating learning materials; its uses should be guided by clear expectations, professional judgment, and school policy. Educators should also teach their students how to use AI ethically, verify outputs for accuracy and bias, and protect student privacy by avoiding sensitive data. Most importantly, assessments should be designed to show genuine student understanding, with AI used transparently and appropriately. The best available published advice concurs that the usage of AI within an educator’s pedagogy significantly enhances middle and secondary school students’ learning. This article offers practical guidance for educators who use or plan to use AI in the classroom, while also highlighting policy recommendations to support effective educational practices.

items.title: Assessment of Internal and External Occupational Exposure to NORM in the Brazilian Oil and Gas Industry
items.abstract: The Oil and Gas industry is one of twelve industries that can involve Naturally Occurring Radioactive Material (NORM), generating a considerable volume of waste in Brazil. The petroleum industry, NORM, is present in geological formations and is accumulated as a function of the process. The most important radionuclides found in scale and sludge are Radium-226 and Radium-228, with activity concentrations that can reach 3,500 Bq/g in the country. The management of NORMs, vital for the safety of workers and the population, as well as for minimizing environmental impacts, encompasses six stages: production and extraction, monitoring, cleaning and decontamination, radiological analysis of NORMs, transportation, and storage. In each phase, workers are exposed to radiological risks through external exposure (gamma radiation) and/or internal exposure (inhalation or ingestion of radioactive particles). Given the large volume of NORM (Naturally Occurring Radioactive Material) and the growing demand for decommissioning offshore platforms in Brazil, which involves handling these materials, the understanding and rigorous application of radiological protection protocols become crucial. Although regulations require occupational health services and individual monitoring, a gap exists in occupational radiological assessments for this sector in the country. Estimated effective doses for the ten workers were comparable and consistently below the LD (Detection Limit) throughout the period of routine NORM exposure. These values fluctuated according to the nature of the work performed. Results confirm that in vitro bioassay is a reliable monitoring method for the oil and gas industry, particularly when integrated with Hp(10) personal dosimetry and stringent safety protocols, ensuring comprehensive monitoring of occupationally exposed workers.

items.title: Auditing a Moving Target: Evidence Anchoring and the Expiry of Fairness Audits of Provider-Served Language Models
items.abstract: Organizations increasingly use large language models (LLMs) for decisions about people, such as hiring, investment and employee evaluation, and rely on them over long periods of time. Fairness audits of such systems, however, are conducted only once. We examine how the biases of LLMs change over time. In a venture screening setting, models from five providers decided whether and how much to invest in startups whose founders differed only in gender, origin and university. We repeated this audit three times over 13 months (248,400 API calls). Study 1 shows that the same model, called under the same identifier one year later, displayed a significantly different bias pattern. Study 2 shows that the successors of retired models carried the same bias as their predecessors, but in a significantly different size and form. Study 3 shows that the bias does not depend on the industry of the startup. A document analysis further shows that providers change and retire models at their discretion, with notice periods of zero to six months. Drawing on these findings, we develop a theory of evidence anchoring. We theorize that bias resides in the model class and persists, whereas audit evidence is anchored to a single model and expires when the provider decides. We derive policy advice for organizations and regulators, namely audits of model classes instead of single models, a version record for every model response, and re-audits triggered by model changes.

items.title: Augmenting Pretrained Language Models with N-gram Embeddings through Incremental Training
items.abstract: As a new scaling technique for large language models, the n-gram embedding improves the base ability of a model while adding almost no inference cost. Mainstream research realizes it through joint training of the n-gram embedding with the backbone, which severely restricts the settings in which an n-gram embedding can be used. We therefore propose training an n-gram embedding onto an existing model through incremental training, to extend where the technique can deliver value. Specifically, we explore several settings of the n-gram embedding under incremental training---the learning rate of the embedding, the vocabulary size, and the injection position---and train an n-gram embedding onto the existing model under the best configuration. Experiments show that the best configuration under incremental training does not fully coincide with that under pretraining; moreover, the incrementally trained knowledge is written predominantly into the n-gram embedding, while the general ability of the backbone is retained throughout this training process.

items.title: Automation, AI and the Changing Skills Demand for University Graduates: A Comparative Qualitative Study across Four Economic Sectors
items.abstract: Automation, digitalization, and, more recently, generative artificial intelligence (gAI) are changing the skill sets employers demand. However, understanding remains limited about how different sector-level stakeholders in developing countries perceive these innovations, and about these technologies' impact on university graduates' employability. The comparative qualitative study draws on 60 interviews with graduates, employer representatives and academics, five of each type per sector, in four Bangladeshi sectors (readymade garments and textiles (RMG); information and communication technology and IT-enabled services (ICT/ITES); banking and financial services; logistics and supply chain management), as well as multi-sector comparative data. Reflexive thematic analysis yielded cross-sector themes, which include framing of technology and specific discussion of AI in ICT/ITES, disciplinary expertise being necessary but no longer sufficient, with digital, data and adaptive capabilities increasingly essential and learned largely outside formal programmes, cross-sector problems with institutional coordination due to curricula lag (the mode and extent of lag varies according to discipline), reasons why these results should not be taken as an indication of job loss and the impact of gAI, as well as sector-specific and generic implications for universities, sectors and employer associations with clear links to the data. Shortcomings include reliance on perceptions, small cell sizes across multiple parameters, and a lack of a worker perspective.

items.title: Awareness, Perceptions, and Practices of Surgical Smoke Management: A Cross-Sectional Study Guided by Behavioral Reasoning Theory
items.abstract: Background Surgical smoke is an occupational health concern for operating theatre personnel because of repeated exposure to potentially hazardous substances. Despite available safety guidance, adherence to surgical smoke management practices remains inconsistent, and the behavioural factors influencing these practices are not well understood. This study aims to examine knowledge, awareness, perceptions, and practices from a behavioural perspective related to surgical smoke safety management among surgeons, anesthetists, and perioperative nurses in an acute hospital in Singapore. Methods A descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted among surgeons, anesthetists, and perioperative nurses who were recruited through convenience sampling. Participants voluntarily completed a validated online questionnaire guided by Westaby’s Behavioral Reasoning Theory. The questionnaire assessed demographics, awareness, perceptions and practices, and surgical smoke-related feedback. Results Among 80 participants, the mean general knowledge score was 1.91 ± 0.76. Most participants demonstrated moderate awareness (80.00%) and moderate perception and practice scores (77.50%). Awareness differed significantly by professional role (p < 0.001), with a significant interaction between professional role and general knowledge (p = 0.030). Nurses had significantly higher perception and practice scores than anesthetists and surgeons (p < 0.001). No significant association was found between awareness and perception and practice scores (p = 0.056). Conclusion The findings indicate persistent gaps in SS knowledge and inconsistent implementation of protective measures. A multifactorial approach combining standardized interdisciplinary education, practical training, engineering controls, and organizational policies is warranted to strengthen SS safety and protect surgical teams and patients from potential exposure.

items.title: Bajillion: Cryptographic Clearing for Micropayments
items.abstract: Much of the web is funded by advertising, a model that erodes as humans delegate browsing to AI agents acting on their behalf. A natural replacement is for agents to pay for what they consume, often a fraction of a cent per request. At the scale of web traffic, this could mean tens or even hundreds of millions of payments per second. We present Bajillion, a clearing protocol for scalable micropayments. A sender signs a payment request, and an untrusted operator answers with a preconfirmation, which promises the receiver that it will be paid. Periodically, the operator closes an epoch by posting only the net effect of its payments on chain. Bajillion guarantees that a malicious operator can only omit payments -- it can never debit a sender beyond what it signed, nor misdirect a transfer. Posted balances are therefore finalized immediately and can be withdrawn. By design, senders never have to raise disputes, making it suitable for ephemeral AI agents. A receiver that is shortchanged can prove that a close omitted a preconfirmed payment, which halts the protocol and lets every user exit with its finalized balance. Requests from different senders can be processed independently, allowing the operator to parallelize up to the number of senders. We capture these guarantees in an ideal functionality for accountable clearing and prove that Bajillion realizes it.
